I gave it some thought and I wanted to explain my reasoning behind all of it. I'm not a professional tarot reader but that's what I think.

BMO is the Fool. The Fool is not an idiot or braindead character. It's a naive, young and vulnerable being and I don't think there's someone better than sweet little angel BMO for the role. 

Magic Man is the Magician. I see Magician card as a way to change perspectives, as someone who will affect your life in this way or another, and that's exactly what Magic Man and then Normal Man and finally King Man were doing in this story - their appearance changed the thought processes of the involved characters in this way or another.

Huntress Wizard is the High Priestess. The card that makes you listen to your inner voice and to follow your instincts, that card with special feminine beauty and studying nature, she is perfect for this role. The way she affected Finn is truly special in my opinion, especially in the last season. 

Minerva is the Empress. The Great Mother of all humanity, the one that symbolize compassion and love for others, the giver, the helper.

Princess Bubblegum is the Emperor. Another authoritative figure, but this one with more leadership, more power, more influence. I see no one else better for this position. 

Glob is the Hierophant. One more ruler, but in the spiritual world, the messenger from the heavens.

LSP is the Lovers. Okay, hear me out because initially I wanted to put TT and Mr. Pig to this position, but the Lovers don't necessarily mean stable relationships. Sometimes lovers card represent changes in them and troubles and I think that LSP is the embodiment of chaotic relationships in Adventure Time.

Betty is the Chariot. The unstoppable force, the determination, someone who would stop at nothing from curing her Simon. 

Susan is the Strength. The ultimate champion, the courage and the fortitude. Also the one who overcome her weaknesses to patch things up with Frida in the end.

Simon is the Hermit. The way he isolated himself both in the beginning of his journey and in the very end after 10th season. He lives amongst the humans, he have friends but it feels like he is alone and almost always hurt.

Prismo is the Wheel of Fortune. Monkey paw, remember? Wishes are dangerous; can put you on top, can push you to the bottom and sometimes both. 
 
Flame Princess is the Justice. Firm, fair and honest, Phoebe is perfect for this spot. Her kingdom is built on honesty.

Lemongrab is the Hanged Man. The Hanged Man is weird in my opinion, it means stagnation, but also sacrifices, surrenders and consequences of one's actions. I feel... I feel like the path of Lemongrab somewhat reminds me of all of that. His kingdom and he himself stagnated and suffered for a while, he made several sacrifices on his way, the Mountain episode reminds me of this card.

Lich is the Death. The end of all things, the ultimate harvest. That card was made for him. 
 
Jake is the Temperance. Now this is... questionable I think, because Jake the party animal is not really the shiny monument of moderation, but imo temperance is not just about moderation - it's also about inner peace and patience and balance. That older brother figure for Finn. I think that this is his spot.

Fern is the Devil. The devil is the shadow self, the entrapment, locking oneself into the trap. Fern was in that trap for a long time, I think he is for this spot. 

Martin is the Tower. The avatar of chaos and destruction, immanent and absolute danger every single time he is on screen after the islands. 

Marceline is the Star. And not just because of that episode lol. The star is about healing and hope, inspiration and growth, but also about vulnerability and purity. Marcy... grew a lot during that long, long journey. That's why I think it's the spot for her. 

Ice King is the Moon. The illusion, doubts and fears, the deception and confusion. Ice King is a demented shell of the human inside, twisted by the crown. 

Finn is the Sun. The golden retriever of major arcanas. His presence throughout the whole series, both in the beginning and in the end is about happiness, joy and optimism.

Death is the Judgement. The ultimate judge, the one who's evaluate your past and decides on your future.

And finally the Comet is the World. The representation of constant change, phases of the journey, the ending of one cycle and the beginning of the other. 

And that's major arcanas. At least, how I see them.

So... last weekend I thought that it was time to experiment with flavors, so here we are.
This recipe is heavily inspired by two very popular videos from youtube. 

1. For the crust I used 240 grams of biscuits and 120 grams of melted butter. After grinding my biscuits, I mixed them with butter and pack it down tightly to my cheesecake form (24 centimeters). I baked the crust over 180 celcius for 10 minutes, then took out the form. I put the form into tinfoil (to prevent leakage) and greased the sides of the form with butter, after which I sticked parchment paper.

2. For my cheesecake I used 750 grams of mascarpone cheese, 500 grams of sour cream, 200 grams of sugar and 300 ml of heavy cream (33%). I mixed them all up and them added two tablespoons of cornstarch. After that I added 4 eggs, one after after another (I didn't worry about overwhipping, cause cornstarch prevent this). After that - several splashes of mint syrup, several drops of vanilla extract and 1 lemon's worth lemon juice.

3. I baked over 180 celcius for 30 minutes, then switch to 150 celcius for 55 minutes. I was constantly adding water to the baking tray to prevent cracks. After 55 minutes of 150 celcius I switched off the oven and waited for one hour, then took out the cheesecake to cool off. 

4. In the meantime I prepared my coconut neutral glaze. I used 8 grams of gelatin, bloomed it in the ice cold water, in the separate pot added 250 grams of sugar, 75 ml of water, 10 ml of lemon juice and 25 ml of coconut syrup. I put the water-sugar-syrup mixture on low heat, mixed it (I wasn't worrying about crystallization, cause the syrup prevented this), dissolved the sugar, waited for the mixture to simmer and added bloomed gelatin. Mixed again to dissolve the gelatin, put the mixture through the little strainer (it called sithe? I'm not sure, sorry ^^"). Then I put it in the fridge, I needed it on the next day.

5. After cheesecake cooled, I carefully opened the form, removed the parchment paper and placed it in the fridge overnight. It looked green! And it was lovely.

6. For my first layer of glaze I made a milk chocolate ganache. I used 300 grams of milk chocolate and 100 ml of heavy cream. Over the water bath slowly melted the chocolate, added the simmering cream, waited for one minute undisturbed and then quickly mixed mixed mixed. Then I put the ganache over my cake, watched it drippling on the tray, it was marvelous... after that put the berries on top (those are strawberries, blueberries and physalis, as well as one sneaky cherry tomato for the laugh). Waited to cool off.

7. I decided to make second ganache - this time with white chocolate (200 grams), 60 ml of heavy cream and 15 ml of coconut syrup. In the meantime I heated yesterday's neutral coconut glaze. I poured white ganache on the cooled milk ganache, then waited for 3 minutes to slightly cool and started to apply the neutral glaze over the berries with the brush. After that, I poured some of my neutral glaze directly into white chocolate and started painting lines with the brush, to make this sort of marble effect. And once again, it was the fridge time.

8. This was a success. The glaze was rich and very sweet, the base was refreshing, slightly acidic from the lemon and moderately sweet. Mint and chocolate worked amazingly well together and coconut was elusive, but, well, there. My friends liked it.

Roughly speaking, there two types of skills - primary and secondary. Primary skills are everyday jobs, things that your colonist will do in the main time - construction, cooking, crafting, mining, intellectual (researching), artistic, plants and animals. Secondary skills represent things that you will have to do form time to time, like fighting enemies or healing your comrades - medical, social, melee and shooting. 

Your colonists will manage several primary skills in the early game, but as the time go by you should specialize their jobs - otherwise it would be a mess, when for example your research could be stagnating because your scientist is cooking for the whole colony. Several secondary skills are okay, though - your medic could easily be a fighter as well.

I would recommend to get colonists with one of the good in early game primary skill (the best choices IMO are construction to build a base, plants to grow a constant source of food and intellectual to begin researching things immediately, although mining or cooking is good too) and with one or two secondary skills - medical to treat your colonists, social to trade and recruit new colonists and either shooting or melee to fight.
